02 / Featured research portfolio · WorldQuant University

From market stress signals
to a testable trading decision.

MScFE 692 — Capstone Review

A two-part group research portfolio investigating how equity co-movement, credit conditions and funding pressure interact—and whether a market-regime filter can improve a pairs-trading strategy.

Presented as collaborative academic research. The reports allocate tasks to Students A, B and C but do not identify Kolapo’s individual allocation; the findings are attributed to the group.

Research progression
Detect → Test → Evaluate

Integrated Early-Warning Risk Management
↓
The Regime-Aware Pairs Trader

Read pairs-trading report ↗
Part I / Integrated Early-Warning Risk Management

Can multiple signals improve risk oversight?

Problem. Standalone measures may miss the interaction between correlated sell-offs, credit widening and funding stress.

Approach. Combined rolling PCA absorption ratios, Baa–Aaa credit spreads, quantile regression, HAR-RV, GARCH/DCC dynamics, funding diagnostics and historical VaR comparisons. Used chronological holdouts and moving-block bootstrap analysis.

Finding. Funding and credit stress were associated with elevated correlation. However, the enhanced credit model’s holdout pinball loss was about 8.57% worse, and HAR-RV error about 16.7% worse, than their respective baselines.

Lesson. A richer dashboard adds context, but model complexity must earn its place through out-of-sample validation.

Part II / The Regime-Aware Pairs Trader

Does standing aside during stress help?

Design. XLK–IYW technology ETF pair, SPY market-regime signal, 2014–2016 formation and 2017–2021 evaluation. Engle–Granger, residual BDS testing and a two-state Markov-switching AR(1) model informed the experiment.

Execution discipline. Filtered calm-state probability above 60%, next-session positions, identical spread rules and 10 bps per-leg turnover costs. A predeclared VIX < 20 fallback addresses regime-model failure.

Finding. The filter avoided all 22 March 2020 trading sessions and reduced maximum drawdown, but increased entries and worsened Sharpe.

Key limitation. Formation cointegration p = 0.634617; the pair failed the test. The trading study is exploratory.

Source: saved execution outputs transcribed in the group’s updated reports, dated October 2026; not independently rerun for this portfolio. Both strategies lost money. The experiment does not establish superior risk-adjusted performance, and excludes several execution and financing frictions. The source reports retain draft verification notes. Next research steps: select a validated cointegrated pair, use walk-forward estimation, test threshold sensitivity and incorporate fuller execution costs.
